interpretation: Batch 2 produced no crash, reboot, hang, or new console error. Six of the seven cases behaved uniformly: the console stayed associated through the 10-second check and disconnected about 35 seconds after association. W-09 (vendor IE length 0) is the exception: it stayed associated through the 10-second check but disconnected at 14.7 seconds, versus 35.6 seconds for the control. That matches the W-06 pattern from Batch 1 (7.3 s and 15.4 s). Two different malformed cases shortening the association lifetime may indicate a generic reject/reset response to malformed information elements, or it may reflect variability in the console's automatic Test Connection flow. It is a behavioral lead, not a memory-safety finding. The batch does not prove that every malformed IE reached the parser; the console may ignore duplicate AP beacons. H-011 remains UNVERIFIED.
authorization: The owner approved the full Batch 2 sequence (control plus W-09-W-14, 25 frames each, 175 frames total) with stop-on-anomaly between cases. The runner stopped only if a station was missing after 10 seconds or a send failed; neither happened.
limitations: One console, one adapter, one driver, and channel 1 only.
The console automatically runs Test Connection on each association and fails at the internet step with 2110-3128 because the AP has no NAT; this timing is part of the observed behavior.
The console may ignore duplicate AP beacons, so no case proves that the malformed IE reached the ARM wlan parser or the Wi-Fi firmware parser.
The W-09 timing difference was observed once (14.7 s); the W-06 difference was 7.3 s and 15.4 s in two runs. The durations are not deterministic.
The same-phy monitor does not capture the AP's own frames; transmission is inferred from netlink acceptance and console behavior.
The two test networks remain saved on the console until the owner removes them.
No crash, hang, or reboot occurred; this is not an exploit or a memory-safety proof.
